blocks.content: The layout root and top-level state composition. Since v4.4 the window is a two-column grid — sidebar | main (header, tab strip, permission card, chat) — with the former right-hand Inspector panel replaced by the Settings modal (⚙ Settings header button, ⌘,, or the command palette). Still owns the sidebar/composer drag-resize machinery (M2), the command palette (⌘K), new-chat shortcut (⌘T), the settings shortcut (⌘,), the shortcut cheatsheet (? or ⌘/), the tab-strip context menu (right-click → open in new window). The tab X and middle-click now remove only the tab from the tab strip; chat records remain in the project list and are not archived or deleted.

startDrag installs window-level pointermove/pointerup listeners; each handle maps pointer position through clamp() to a Layout patch (sidebar 180–480, composer 80–300). applyLayout debounces settings persistence to one write per 400 ms and applies immediately for zero-lag feedback. The sidebar collapse renders a 44px rail with an expand button; the inspector column, its resize handle, and its collapsed flag are retired from the UI (v4.4) — settings.json layout keys of the old shape are still tolerated on read.

settingsOpen state renders <Settings> with the same data props the Inspector received plus onDeleteProject (wired to useXtrac.deleteProject) for the Project → Danger zone. The modal component stays mounted while closed so the last-visited section is remembered.
Everything below comes from this hook — see its own article.
The M2 resize system; layout persists in settings.json under `layout`.
⌘K entries: new project, open folder, Settings (⌘,), new chat, shortcuts, and chat switching.
